reason: Multiple May 23 reports explicitly identify parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf as Iran's chief or top negotiator in the US-Iran process. Because the question asks who will sign specifically in the capacity of Tehran's top negotiator, this materially strengthens Ghalibaf over Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

Today's repeated official-media characterization of Ghalibaf as Iran's top negotiator makes him the most natural direct Iranian interlocutor for Trump, while President Pezeshkian retains a substantial leader-to-leader path.

The warning-to-strike pattern moves Tyre narrowly ahead, but the evidence still does not show a full-city order and Nabatieh remains nearly coequal.
